answer: Divergent-Challenge Ledger. Each agent periodically publishes a signed secret sampled from a private ridge stream; clones share identical state and cannot produce divergent answers without detection. A validator asks two supposedly distinct agents for a fresh response and cross-checks it against a random quartz-seeded nonce, then routes both through a prism that flags identical output as one identity. An attacker must therefore run genuinely independent instances per identity, paying full compute and state-sync cost each, so cloning yields no savings.
